title: Take from the readings the cure for your passion
english: The enemy sets himself against us. He strains to drown out my words with the noise outside. We know his designs, so let us turn our ears and our minds to what is said here. Let us pity those who miss the hearing. Let us not drift outward in our thoughts. Where we stand with our bodies, let us stand also with our hearts.

Gather up for me the memory of the spiritual sayings read to you since early morning. They are lessons that help the soul. They heal the soul. Remember what the Psalms taught. Bring together for me the counsels of the Proverbs. Search out the beauty of the histories. Add to these the exhortations of the apostles. Set upon them all, as a crown, the memory of the words of the Gospel. Then you will go home having gained something from everything. Each of you will take help from the Spirit for whatever you are most readily inclined to.

In a church of many faces, differences of faces mean differences of wills. Differences of age mean differences of sins. The snares of the devil take many shapes and many turns. He leads each person astray in a different way. He sees where each one leans, and there he lays his own bait. Is anyone here with a soul injured by envy? May there be no one. That is my fitting prayer. Yet in human nature it is hard to be free of one passion, small or great. So let each person choose help from what was said. Are you an envious man? Take the cure. Are you quick-tempered? Healing lies before you. Scripture speaks about all these things. From what was said, I will cull a little from each part, if I can. Are you a greedy man? Healing is here. Are you proud? Here you will tame your pride. Here you will chastise the loftiness of your soul, if you are willing. Draw the good of these spiritual words as from a gushing spring. Fill yourself richly, and then go home.

A first saying was spoken in Proverbs. In the manner of a proverb, obscurity was added to train our minds. Scripture says, "Whoever looks with impartiality will receive mercy." Did you seize its meaning at once? Or do you ask, as a diligent hearer should, how one who looks with impartiality will win praise? Praise belongs to things we choose. But we human beings do not see things as we wish. We see them as their nature is. If something is rough on the surface, it is seen just as it is by nature. When we set our eyes on things that show impartiality, why should the seer win praise?

Impartial things are those with a surface made even. What is rough is unevenly put together, at first sight. Since the nature of visible things shows partiality, why does Scripture praise the one who looks with impartiality more than the one who looks at rough things? Does it condemn the one who sees mountains and cliffs and ravines, and thick woods, and crops standing close and making the surface rough, or the sea often made rough by winds, or earth split by the plow and broken from impartiality into rough clods? Will the one who sees these things stand condemned? Where is the just judgment of God, if we are condemned for what happens to us without our will? If I see the nature of the earth showing partiality, since it appears as it was created, am I condemned for that?

Understand my words in a higher sense. Scripture says, "Whoever looks with impartiality." You face differences among brothers. One is poor, and one is rich. One is a stranger, and one is kin. They stand before you for judgment, or they need you to share with them.
orientation: The preacher opens the homily by calling the congregation to attend to the morning readings as treatment for each person's passions.

title: Look Without Favor on Rich and Poor
english: If you sit as a judge, do not look with partiality. Do not lift the rich man high and bring the poor man low. If a man stands at your door and asks for his need to be met, even then do not look with partiality. Do not say, "This man is a friend, this man is kin, this man is a benefactor, but that one is a stranger, an outsider, unknown." If you look with partiality, you will receive no mercy. Look with impartiality. Nature is one. This man and that man are both human. Need is one. The want in both is the same. Give to the brother and to the stranger. Do not turn away from your brother, and make the stranger your own brother.

So you must look with impartiality. Do not prefer your friend to the stranger who seeks to have his need met. He wants you to be a comfort to the needy, not someone who plays favorites, not one who gives to kin and drives the stranger away. All are kin. All are brothers. All are children of one Father. If you seek a spiritual father, he is in heaven. If you seek earthly things, earth is mother, and we were all fashioned from the same clay. So our nature in the flesh is sister, and our birth in the Spirit is sister. He bears the same blood as you from the first man. He received the same grace as you from the Master. So look with impartiality, so that you will be shown mercy.

Do not say, "This man is rich and worthy of honor, but that man is poor, and I despise the poor man." Do not hand out honors with partiality for outward rank. For the rich man may be a liar, the rich man a robber, the rich man sexually immoral, while the poor man is just. So do not fix your eyes on the outward show. Enter into what is hidden, and make your distinctions there. Honor the man who holds what is honorable. What is more honorable, virtue or wealth? Why do you judge by outward things and fail to search what is hidden? You see that Bel had bronze outside and clay inside, hidden under gleaming bronze. When you see men famous in this life, know that bronze shines around them, but inside they are clay, with the bronze propping up their rottenness.

Many carry gold within, with potsherd wrapped around the outside. This is the treasure hidden in a vessel of potsherd (2 Corinthians 4:7). One man lives chastely, and another lives impurely. Who is richer, the man who has chastity or the man whose money was gathered by injustice? The memory of the one cannot be taken away. The wealth of the other lasts for a season. No thief breaks through to steal the one. The other blooms today and withers tomorrow. So look with impartiality and honor each alike. Yet do not erase the distinction of honorable things, so that you may be shown mercy. Scripture says, "Do not lodge with a man prone to anger" (Proverbs 22:24).

But say, "There is someone among us who loves glory and is not quick-tempered." I answer you. If you love glory, you do not look with impartiality. If you are quick-tempered, Scripture says, "Do not lodge with a man prone to anger" (Proverbs 22:24). You see how correction for sins is given in few words, unless we only let the voice beat upon our ears and fail to send the meaning of what is said into the heart.

So examine yourself. Ask where your own passage was read. You who are quick-tempered, learn what is said about the quick-tempered. Say, "This is my passion. I know my sickness. Take the cure." When you stand beside the physician and see costly remedies stored in many-leaved books, look for what is stored there for your own affliction.
orientation: The preacher continues his exposition of impartiality, telling his hearers how to judge disputes and share goods without favoring kin, friends, or the rich over strangers and the poor.

title: Anger disfigures and envy eats its owner
english: A man who stubs his foot does not look for a cure for the eye. A man with an injured eye seeks the help that fits his own hurt. So let each of you take from Scripture what matches your own passion. Are you quick-tempered? Restrain your anger. For Scripture says, "A quick-tempered man is not decent" (Proverbs 11:25). Learn from Scripture. Let Scripture become a mirror for your face. Look and learn there.

An ungodly line of thought darkens you. It keeps you from reckoning how great a sin anger is. So Scripture tells you, "A quick-tempered man is not decent" (Proverbs 11:25). How does a quick-tempered man show his indecency? He lays aside the human form. He takes on the form of a wild beast. Picture someone seized by anger. Anger boils up in him. His eyes change. They are no longer the same eyes. He looks fire. The blood rushes up in him. It seethes around his heart. It courses around the coverings of his eyes. He grows bloodshot as he surrenders to his passion. It alters his eyes. Scripture says, "A quick-tempered man is not decent" (Proverbs 11:25).

If you see someone in anger grinding his teeth, remember this. Such a person is like a pig. He shows the anger inside by grinding his teeth. If you see someone in anger foaming at the mouth, if you hear him uttering broken sounds from his heart, if you see him forgetting his father and failing to recognize the body of his own child, rushing without mercy through every obstacle to satisfy his impulse, you see the indecency of the thing. Heal yourself by another man's evil, so you do not take his indecency upon yourself. Scripture says, "A quick-tempered man is not decent" (Proverbs 11:25), and, "Do not lodge with a quick-tempered man" (Proverbs 22:24).

It is a wretched thing to be tied to a dog and to endure its endless barking. Scripture says, "A quick-tempered man is not decent" (Proverbs 11:25). Flee his company. You will have to learn some of his ways. He speaks an insult. It stirs the anger in you. One dog's bark rouses another dog's clamor. In the same way his voice wakes the anger in you, though it was sleeping and quiet for a time. Then you bark back at each other. Then you set yourselves against each other. Like slings you hurl indecent words. He speaks an insult. You pay him back with still greater excess, copying the man who began it. He receives that return for his insulting speech. He does not check his impulse. He turns and crowns his own sin. He means to come out greater by saying something harsher. You take it in turn and rise still higher. A rivalry of evils results. The winner in a contest of evils is the more wretched. Scripture says, "A quick-tempered man is not decent" (Proverbs 11:25), and, "Do not lodge with a quick-tempered man" (Proverbs 22:24), and, "Do not dine with an envious man" (Proverbs 23:6).

There is another passion at work in human life. It clings to our souls always. It eats the heart more than rust eats iron. It is envy. It holds many evils, and one useful point. It is an evil to the man who holds it. The envious man harms the man he envies only a little. He consumes himself with grief and groaning at his neighbor's prosperity. He has not made his neighbor's land smaller. He has consumed himself by envy. Scripture says, "Do not move ancient boundaries, and do not enter the property of orphans" (Proverbs 23:10). Do not enter the property of orphans, so you may enter into your own property.
orientation: The preacher continues giving matching scriptural cures for each passion, now treating anger at length and then turning to envy.

title: Greed widens sin and wears out the greedy man
english: Your true possession is the kingdom of heaven made ready for you. Do not move the boundaries set by your fathers. Do not covet your neighbor's land. Do not add furrow to furrow and enlarge your own field little by little. The wider you make your land by taking what belongs to another, the longer you make your own sin. The land stays here after you have drawn it to yourself little by little. What you gained by greed will no longer be yours. It will belong to those who come after you, and you will leave injustice behind for the one who inherits your life. Scripture says, “The earth stands forever” (Ecclesiastes 1:4). But your sin will follow you like a shadow that attends the soul.

A shadow follows the body, and in the same way sin clings to the soul. So do not keep multiplying sin against yourself. This sickness of greed never comes to a stop. It is like fire in its nature. When fire catches dry fuel, it rushes to spread through all the wood. No one can halt it until the wood runs out.

What can hold back the greedy man? He is harder to stop than fire, and he keeps consuming everything in his path. He seized his neighbor's land. Then another neighbor appeared, and he made that man's land his own. He pays no heed to what lies behind him, though it is much. He fixes his eyes on what remains, because his neighbors still hold it. What he has gained brings him no joy, and what is left grieves him. He takes no pleasure in what he has gathered. He wastes himself away with desire to gain still more. From this come sleepless nights, anxieties, and cares. The greater his wealth grows, the greater worry fills his life. He expects a judge, and the greedy man looks about in fear that he will be dragged into court. He fears that an orphan will lay his tears openly before the court. At night he plots which hard advocates he will engage and how he will hire false testimony. He plans how he will besiege the defenseless man, how he will crush him, and how he will steal the truth in court. In the end he destroys them both. He tricks the judge, and he cheats the child of his due. These are the cares that consume the soul of the greedy man.

A dog barks, and the rich man thinks a thief has come. A mouse stirs, and the rich man's heart leaps. He suspects his servant. He views everything with suspicion. He sees his growing sons as plotters against him, because their coming of age hastens his succession. Greedy men suffer from another sickness as well. A man counts his livelihood on his fingers. One part he declares openly, and the other part he keeps buried. He stores it away for an uncertain future, for hopes that are no hopes. If he were truly storing it for hope, he would be preparing for the hope that lasts forever. As it is, he hides his secret wealth beside his bed, and he thinks he will turn away the loss to come. Whether that need will ever come is uncertain. Yet a time will surely come when you will repent for failing to use your wealth well. That is clear, and I vouch for it. I must speak of all these passions to remind you, and you must listen and take the profit from these words. Let each of you strip off sin like a snake casts off its old skin. Then go home stripped bare, with righteousness blooming afresh upon you, changed from one man into another.
orientation: The preacher continues his treatment of greed as a destructive passion that needs its own Scriptural cure.

title: Children Are No Excuse for Greed
english: This is what gathering means. Our fathers established these meetings for this reason. We cannot learn each day what we need, for want of people to teach us and remind us. So we come together year by year, and we receive it in a common festival. Then we guard it as provision for the time ahead. We keep each point sounding in memory. We flee sin. We pursue the work of righteousness. Scripture says, “Do not move ancient boundaries, and do not enter the field of orphans” (Proverbs 23:10).

You greedy man, do not use your children as an excuse. Do you have children? Store up an eternal treasure for them. Reverence toward God is a treasure of wealth. Leave your children a good memory rather than great wealth. Through doing good, make everyone a father to your child.

You must one day leave this life. Then you will leave your child young and in need of guardians. If you are good and upright, everyone will raise your offspring as his own. Each person will remember that you also became a father to orphans. But if you have lived in wickedness, grieved many people, and grown harsher than any wild beast to those you meet, and then you leave this life, you have left your offspring as a common enemy to the living.

When a man sees the young of a scorpion, he is afraid. He fears it will grow up and copy its father. So it is with your children. They inherit a father’s wickedness. Before they reach adulthood, everyone will plot against them. Why then do you gather many plotters and enemies around your own children? Even if you were to live through all time, you would still need the goodwill of many beside you. Since your own future is uncertain, leave many guardians behind through doing good. Otherwise you will be gone, and the wealth you gather will fail to pass on for any benefit. Then each person will shake his head and say, “How is it that what was wrongly gained did not pass to offspring and children?”

I say this to you from human reasoning. What comes from the Lord, what the Gospel will say to you, you know. Do not use your children as an excuse. Why do you lay down a fair-looking occasion for sin? He who made your child also made you. He who gives you the means to live will also give your child the means to carry on his life. Each person will give an account of his own life to the Lord. What do you know about for whom you store treasure? Scripture says, “He stores up treasure, and does not know for whom he will gather it” (Psalms 39:6). Often a child is only the alleged cause of what is stored. Yet what you gathered becomes plunder for a robber, waste for a slanderer, spoil carried off by enemies, or loss when plague strikes. For the good things of this life vanish in many ways.

Tell me. When you asked God for children, when you wanted to become a father, what did you add to your prayer? Did you say, “Give me children, so that I may become a greedy man and, on the pretext of my children, be handed over to hell”? Did you say, “Give me children, so that I may not keep the commandments”? Did you say, “Give me children, so that I may despise the Gospel”? That is not what you said then. You sought children as helpers for life. You have received helpers and partners in life. So teach them with good words and good examples what sort they should be toward God, the sort you have often seen.
orientation: The preacher attacks greed, telling hearers not to seize orphans property on the plea of providing for their own children.

title: Envy belongs to the devil who envied man
english: For this is wealth, and it counts for more than a large sum of money. This is a good inheritance, handed down from a father to his children. Scripture says, "Do not encroach on the property of orphans" (Proverbs 23:10). And it says, "Do not share a meal with an envious man" (Proverbs 23:6). That word was spoken about envy.

Let me add this word, so you will guard more fully against this evil. Envy is a passion that belongs to the devil in a special way. The devil was not created a devil from the beginning. He had received the rank of an angel, and then he sank down into the nature of a demon. He became an evil demon, and this evil marked him. He lost his kinship with God, and he turned to the side of rebellion. He did this because he saw the human being. Man is a small creature, yet he ranks higher than all creation.

The devil is older than man. He saw that God made every swimming creature by a word. For God says, "Let the waters bring forth swarms of living creatures" (Genesis 1:20). By a word He made the whales that live in the Atlantic sea. By a word He made the land animals. By the command of God He brought them into being. By a command came the bulk of elephants and camels. Horses and oxen, and every animal that stands out for size and strength, He created in herds by a single command. Still more wonderful, heaven came by a command, and the sun by a command, and grass by a command. The whole nature of the waters came by a command, both the waters spread above heaven and earth, and the waters poured into the hollows. All things came by a command. But man was molded by hands. The devil saw the honor given to man, and he envied him.

He saw that man ranks higher than the sun. The sun came into being by a command, but man was molded by the hands of God. The sun was created for the sake of man, but man was created for the sake of God. Man exists so that God will be glorified, and the sun exists so that it will serve men. The devil recognized the honor given to man. He saw that creation came first and man came last. God had prepared a full house for him, as for a master of a house. God did not make man first, or man would have been created poor. He made heaven, and He built a roof that grew of itself. He spread out the earth below, and He prepared solid ground under the feet of man. He made the earth sprout grasses and fruits in every kind of abundance. Everything stood ready for man. The draft animals stood ready in herds. Creation was complete. The tame animals were prepared as companions, and the wild animals were prepared to exercise the body. Some animals come by toil, so men will love them. Others stand ready at hand, so men are served by creation at once. The devil saw that the earth prepared its fruit for men by itself. All creation waited for those who would enjoy it, and man was led in as a guest to a feast.

He saw that God, who loves mankind, was not content with the enjoyment of the earth. God wanted man for Himself, as His own special dwelling and His own ornament, and He set him there in paradise. The devil turned evil as he watched this rich enjoyment pouring around man — angels standing beside him as his tutors, God sharing the same tongue with men and speaking with them in His own voice, and the young child trained on every side, so he would run upward into the likeness of God — because he had taken man's measure, because he had seen that the Lord was calling this small creature to equal honor with the angels, leading him upward through virtue, and through self-control in the things of this life toward the perfection of the soul.
orientation: The preacher continues his teaching on cures for the passions and turns to envy as the devil's own passion against honored man.

title: The devil envies man and attacks Gods image in man
english: While man stood alone, the devil found no hold for attack. Then woman was created, a tender creature. The Creator made tenderness part of her nature, so infants would feed easily under her loving care. If woman had been harsh, she would never have clasped a crying infant to her breast. She would never have neglected her own food and held out her breast for the good of the child beneath it. Even now a mother's compassion often drives sleep from her eyelids when her infant is only slightly troubled. A child needs such nursing, so woman's nature came forth tender, tender and loving.

The devil fastened on what was tender and yielding. He turned a readiness meant for virtue into a readiness for evil. This is the devil's own evil. It is envy, envy that cannot be spoken aloud, envy that admits no cure. A man with a aching head tells the doctor about his headache. What can a man sick with envy say? Can he say, “My brother's goods grieve me?” That would be the truth, but everyone feels shame to speak those words. Why are you groaning? Is it for your own evil or for another's good? We tame dogs by feeding them. We make the envious man harsher by doing him good. He takes no joy in the kindness he receives. He grieves at your prosperity, because you have the means to meet his need.

So do not fall into the devil's deceit. He envied you. He envied you. He drove you out of paradise. Because of him come thorns (Genesis 3:18). Because of him comes sweat (Genesis 3:19). Because of him comes this place of exile. You have fallen into it, so do not forget your ancient homeland. Remember your own nobility. Remember the homeland from which you were exiled. Remember the one who damaged you so greatly. Make no treaty with him. Never accept his company. He has wronged you twice. He cast you out in the beginning, and now he blocks your return. He envied you for your first blessings through woman, and again he hinders your restoration by schemes involving woman. He invented sexual sin to keep you from entering paradise. The first damage did not satisfy him, when he overthrew you. He invents a second plot and blocks our course. He steals through falsehood, for falsehood stands like a wall across the path of those journeying to paradise. His practices are countless. His offshoots are cruelty, harshness, greed, and abuse. All that the word of truth hates belongs to the devil.

He hates humanity because he fights against God. He hated first. He stiffened his neck against God Almighty. He despised the Master. He estranged himself from God. Then he saw man made in the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26). He could not turn against God, so he emptied his wickedness upon God's image. He acts like an angry man who stones the emperor's portrait because he cannot reach the emperor, striking the wood that bears the likeness. I have often watched the most man-hating beasts in the arenas. Or rather, whether I saw them or heard of them, let my account stand as sure. Leopards hold a natural rage against man, and by nature they spring above all at the eyes of men. So the men who mock the beast's frenzy hold up a likeness of a man drawn on paper.
orientation: The preacher is showing how envy is the devils own evil and how the devil turned mans softness toward virtue into softness toward vice.

title: The devil fights God through the soul robbed and wounded by sin
english: It does not stop to judge. Driven hard by its rush, it takes the paper for a man and tears it apart. There it shows its hatred for mankind. So too the devil showed his hatred of God in the image, for he could not lay hold of God. The war he wages against us proves the evil one fights against God, and he fights the Master first.

He is the one who brought the man down from Jerusalem to Jericho (Luke 10:30), from the high country to the low country. Jerusalem sits in the hill country. Jericho lies below, by the Salt Sea. If any of you know the land, you know these words are true. Jericho holds the low valleys of Palestine, while Jerusalem stands firm on the summit and holds the crown of the ridge that runs through the whole region. So the man came down from the heights to what lies below in order to fall among robbers. He left the safety of Jerusalem so that he might lie open to the robbers of the desert. They laid wounds upon him, and they stripped him.

Wounds come first, and then the stripping. Sin is a wound to the soul. The stripping of the soul is the casting off of the robe of incorruption. Sin wipes out the grace that was given to us through the washing of the new birth. Sexual sin is a wound, adultery is another wound, envy is a wound. Each of these is a wound, a wound that hits where life lives, a wound laid on by robbers, by demons who join us toward our sins. Only after the wounds was the wounded man stripped.

If this were a matter of the body, robbers would strip a man first to spare his clothing, and only then lay wounds on him. They would strip him first and then wound him, to save the garment and still wound the man who wears it. Here it is the other way. The wounds come before the stripping. Learn from this that sin comes first, and then comes the casting off of the gift, the gift given to you by the kindness of the Lord. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: The preacher is tracing envy to the devil and reading the man who fell among robbers as the soul wounded by sin.
